title: A Gaussian blend at 5.43 km/s predicts the HD 69830 bisector change within 1.1 m/s under a fixed line model
abstract: We test an extra line-shape constraint on a published model of the HD 69830 twilight velocity excursion. An equal-width Gaussian blend fitted to velocity and width predicts a bisector change of -37.341 m/s. The measured change is -38.427 m/s. A second fit matches velocity and width but predicts -60.310 m/s. The third measure distinguishes these two nominal models. A different depth cut gives -38.171 m/s for the lower-separation fit. The agreement depends on the line model, continuum fit and assumed true velocity change. No event error, full line profile, sky spectrum or independent instrument confirms the cause. We find no new planet. Original code, aggregate evidence, source hashes and external retrieval steps are included. Source records are excluded.

display.caption: Predicted and measured bisector changes. The right panel retains only sensitivity settings that match the fitted velocity and width to the stated tolerance. These are model tests, not confidence intervals.
